children: Mexico's inflation likely picked in early October as summertime electricity subsidies ended in a number of cities, contributing to higher energy costs. The consumer price index is expected to have risen 0.38% in the first two weeks of the month, nudging the 12-month inflation rate up to 3.59% from 3.49% in the second half of September, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. Core CPI, which excludes energy and perishable foods, is seen up 0.17% in the two-week period, leaving the 12-month core rate practically unchanged at 3.70%. National statistics institute Inegi is scheduled to report mid-October inflation on Thursday. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
